title: entity_subsystem_test is flaky against the shared TestHarness: two independent cross-binary races (tenant_default schema_migrations 23505, and resetTestData deleting a live test's instance_projections mid-test)
discovered_during: WF03-gh439-testwiring-20260806 step q159 (ISS-0159 / GH #480 + ISS-0160 / GH #481) — surfaced while running zig build test-integration-exp repeatedly to confirm the 12/12 result was stable rather than a single lucky run
symptom:
`zig build test-integration-exp` does not produce a stable result. Measured over 10 consecutive runs with the ISS-0159/ISS-0160 fixes applied: 8 runs 12/12, 2 runs degraded (10/12 and 11/12). The degradation is NOT in the entity command path — it is in TestHarness.init()/resetTestData and reproduces on the pre-fix baseline too, where the same file fluctuated 9/12..10/12 across 10 runs rather than sitting at a stable 10/12.

Two distinct signatures were captured:

Race A — migration ledger collision on tenant_default:
  POSTGRES ERROR C23505 duplicate key value violates unique constraint "schema_migrations_schema_version_uq"
  Key (schema_name, version)=(tenant_default, 1137_iss0156_entity_instance_projection_backfill.sql) already exists.
  runMigrationsForSchema (tenant_default) failed: error.MigrationFailed
  -> src/db/migrations.zig:393 runForSchema <- tests/integration/helpers.zig:196 <- helpers.zig:919 TestHarness.init
Once one block trips this, every LATER block in the same binary fails at TestHarness.init with error.OutOfOrderMigration (src/db/migrations.zig:309), cascading a single race into 5 failed blocks (7/12 observed).

Race B — resetTestData removing a live test's fixture rows:
  [default] (warn): killIdleConnections: unexpected cross-owner idle connections remain, count=1
  resetTestData: cross-owner idle connections remain; continuing
  -> src/event_store/store.zig:330 StoreError.InstanceNotFound <- src/entities/commands.zig updateRecord
  ("EXP-202: Update entity record") and, in the same run,
  -> try std.testing.expect(r2.is_duplicate) fails at entity_subsystem_test.zig:525
  ("EXP-202: Create record idempotency")
Both are consistent with a concurrently-running sibling harness truncating instance_projections / the event tables while this binary's test is mid-flight: the synthetic entity-type instance created by getOrCreateEntityTypeInstance disappears (InstanceNotFound), and the first call's idempotency row disappears so the replay is no longer recognised as a duplicate.
root_cause: Race B (the cause of BOTH observed failure signatures) is a lock-SCOPE defect, not a missing lock. TestHarness.init() held the bpm_test_migrations_public advisory lock across migrations -> resetTestData -> ensureDefaultOidcSeeds, then explicitly released it before conn.begin() and before returning the harness. That made init mutually exclusive only with other inits. resetTestData() issues unconditional DELETEs against instance_projections, events, process_definitions and nine other tables in the shared tenant_default schema that every integration binary provisions -- so binary B's init deleted binary A's fixture rows while A's test was live. A's per-test transaction does not protect it: READ COMMITTED means each statement sees B's committed deletes. Hence StoreError.InstanceNotFound (synthetic entity-type instance vanishes) and expect(r2.is_duplicate) failing (idempotency row vanishes). Race A: src/db/migrations.zig:490 was the ONLY writer to public.schema_migrations without ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING (migrate.zig, helpers.zig and GBL-133's two inserts all have one). The ISS-0144 recheck-under-lock already closes the check-then-act window, but the bare INSERT turned any residual race into a binary-wide cascade: one C23505 aborts the transaction, then every later TestHarness.init() fails with error.OutOfOrderMigration.
reproduction:
Requires BPM_TEST_DB_URL pointing at a real PostgreSQL.

  for i in $(seq 1 12); do zig build test-integration-exp --summary all; done

-> most runs report 12/12; roughly 1 in 5 reports 10/12 or 11/12 (occasionally 7/12 when Race A cascades). Grep the output for `OutOfOrderMigration`, `schema_version_uq`, `InstanceNotFound`, or `cross-owner idle connections` to classify which race fired.

The same loop on the pre-ISS-0159/0160 baseline gives 9/12..10/12 rather than a stable 10/12, confirming the instability predates those fixes.
impact:
`test-integration-exp` cannot be used as a reliable gate: a green run is not evidence the entity subsystem is correct, and a red run is not evidence it is broken. This is the ISS-0143 problem in a different place — a signal that cannot be trusted in either direction. Worse, Race A's cascade means one race converts into five apparent failures, which invites misdiagnosis of unrelated blocks (exactly the ISS-0106 pattern where a deadlock surfaced as an unrelated-looking failure in a different binary).

Because the entity blocks are among the newest, any future regression in src/entities/ will be indistinguishable from this flake until it is fixed.
candidate_resolution:
Diagnose separately from ISS-0151 / GH #483 (different schema, different mechanism, same error code — do not fold them together without reproducing under conditions that falsify the other's stated cause, per the ISS-0091 anti-pattern).

For Race A: apply the ISS-0144 remedy shape to the tenant_default path — re-verify `(schema_name, version)` with a fresh query taken AFTER the advisory lock is granted, immediately before applying, and skip cleanly (COMMIT, not ROLLBACK) if a concurrent holder already recorded it. Also worth checking why a MigrationFailed on one block leaves the ledger in a state that makes every subsequent TestHarness.init in the same binary return OutOfOrderMigration — that cascade is its own defect and turns a 1-block flake into a 5-block one.

For Race B: identify which binary/step truncates instance_projections while a sibling is mid-test, and make that truncation take the same advisory lock the harness uses, or scope it to the owner's own tenant schema.

Do not resolve either by adding retries, sleeps, or by relaxing the entity assertions — the assertions are correct and the entity fixes under ISS-0159/ISS-0160 are independently verified by mutation checks.
notes: Filed rather than fixed inline per the Issue Queue protocol: this is shared test-infrastructure concurrency work with its own root cause(s), outside the src/entities/ scope of step q159, and step q159's own acceptance (12/12, zero leaks) is independently demonstrated — including three mutation checks proving each entity fix is load-bearing. Enqueued QUEUED on run WF03-gh439-testwiring-20260806.
resolution: 1. Hold the bpm_test_migrations_public advisory lock for the whole harness lifetime: acquire in init(), release in deinit() after rollback() and before close(). This serializes whole binaries rather than just their inits. 2. Added ON CONFLICT (schema_name, version) DO NOTHING to the migrations.zig ledger insert (defence in depth).
verification: Reproduced FIRST: 3 concurrent test-integration-exp invocations gave 10/12, 11/12, 12/12 with both signatures present (serial runs were 6/6 clean -- the races are cross-binary). After the fix: 3 concurrent runs all 12/12 with zero race signatures; a 4-way stress run all 12/12 in 18s with no 55P03 lock timeouts. Pre-existing failures in test-integration-iss0602-cross (2 pass/1 fail) and test-integration-tm (3 pass/11 fail) were measured identically WITH and WITHOUT the fix, so they are unrelated to this change (they belong to the #482/ISS-0150 family of known mass integration failures on main).
prevention: src/design/iss0162_test_harness_cross_binary_races.md records why the lock must span the harness lifetime rather than just init, so a future narrowing does not silently reopen this. The unlock is catch{}-guarded and a session-level advisory lock is also released when the connection drops, so no failure path can strand it.
